The money will be used to equip Ukrainian forces to use lethal weaponry against Russia, the EU's EU defence chief Marco Antonio said on Tuesday, as part of the EU's counter-offensive. "The US's decision to deploy tanks in Ukraine is not a result of our EU defence policy," Antonio said. "It is the result of the EU's policy of'resistance to aggression and terrorism' for many years." Asked whether Nato's first-ever force in Europe would be in Ukraine, which has its own armed forces and is not considered "part of NATO" by the EU, Antonio said: "I don't know when Nato would start. But I think it will start in mid-February, when it is ready." He added: "We have to put a lot of pressure on Russia and the West to ensure that they do not start the counter-offensive there." The EU's foreign ministers said the EU was making an effort to "create a credible, credible, and credible Ukraine". EU Defence Secretary Pravda Agus said the plan was "a very significant step" in the right direction. "It is an important step and it is already making a major contribution to the current situation of the situation in Ukraine.
It is also an important step to restore our international credibility and legitimacy and to ensure that our military partners can put an end to this conflict.
The EU is also using the deal to assist Ukraine in moving its weapons to Ukraine. The country is also looking to buy up to 300,000 rounds of ammunition this year.
In exchange, NATO and its allies will provide Ukraine with 10,000 artillery shells, said the Russian Foreign Ministry on Monday.

Russia's Russian Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu said the EU was ready to supply Ukraine with up to 300,000 of its own 120,000-round ammunition, which is "sufficient to protect the international security of the EU and its members".
